title: Veir Raises $110M in Series C Funding to Scale Superconducting Power Systems for AI Data Centers
key_facts: Veir raised $110 million in Series C funding to move its superconducting power delivery from testing to commercial deployment in AI data centers.
Matter Venture Partners and Tyche Partners co-led; LG Technology Ventures, Gates Frontier, Sabanci Climate Ventures and Hui Capital took part.
Total capital raised is $225 million, per the company, which is based in Woburn, Mass. and was founded in 2019.
The system combines superconducting cables with cryogenic cooling, controls and monitoring; initial focus is power inside a customer's facility, behind the meter.
Veir has demonstrated a 3-megawatt system and is working with customers on commercial deployments and reference designs.
Funding will expand manufacturing, product portfolio and commercial operations.
quote_evidence: Veir has raised $110 million in Series C funding to move its superconducting power-delivery technology from testing into commercial deployment for AI data centers.
The round brings Veir’s total capital raised to $225 million, according to the Woburn, Mass.-based company.
why_it_matters_hint: Money to take a compact power-delivery technology toward commercial use in AI data centers.
